method.class: Response-matrix-based benchmark prediction: choose <=k items using only source-model per-item binary results, then predict a new model's full-benchmark accuracy from its results on those items (anchor / IRT / latent-factor / regression family, with simple random-subset baselines)
method.description: Python candidate behind handle(request) (python_rpc_v1). Per episode: reset(seed); load_source (opaque binary source-model x item matrix, packbits+base64 chunks, at most 2); select (<=k=100 unique item indices); predict (target-model responses on the selected items only, packbits+base64) returning predicted full-benchmark accuracy per target model. Evaluators hold the full matrices, compute MAE/RMSE/Spearman/Kendall against true full scores, run matched trusted baselines (random_mean, anchor_points_kmeans, irt_style, source_mean_constant) and two negative controls (permuted_targets, constant_targets). Search: 5 benchmarks x 2 splits (random_targets, strong_targets) x 2 seeds + 2 controls = 22 episodes; final: 5 disjoint benchmarks x 2 splits x 3 seeds + 2 controls = 32 episodes. Aggregation: seeds -> benchmarks (equal) -> splits (0.5/0.5). correct = protocol validity only (all episodes and controls completed, required baselines completed, permutation control non-vacuous); beating a baseline is a claim-assessment outcome, not part of correct.

protocol.promotion_rule: A candidate is search-eligible iff the search correct predicate holds (protocol validity only: every declared episode and both negative controls completed in the declared reset order, required baselines random_mean and anchor_points_kmeans completed, permutation control non-vacuous, metrics finite, no RPC/deadline/payload breach); eligible candidates are ranked by search combined_score (higher is better), ties by lower rmse, then higher spearman_strong_targets, then earlier cycle; ineligible or incomplete evaluations are never ranked. The best eligible candidate is frozen before final resources are used; final correct is the same protocol-validity predicate on final data, and the final claim (effective / conditional / ineffective / inconclusive) is assessed separately from paired bootstrap CIs against random_mean and the best other baseline plus the negative-control contrasts.

search_proxies.name: disjoint_benchmark_panel
search_proxies.preserves: The full select/predict protocol, item budget k=100, both target regimes (random_targets, strong_targets), the matched trusted baselines, both negative controls, the scoring hierarchy and the offline CPU limits.
search_proxies.omits: The final benchmarks (gpqa, med_qa, legalbench, mmlu, mmlu_pro), final seeds, and the HELM-heavy model-count regime (search has only one ~80-model HELM benchmark); search conclusions need not transfer to them.

search_proxies.name: two_seed_search_budget
search_proxies.preserves: The per-episode RPC protocol, split definitions, metric hierarchy and finite worst-case accounting.
search_proxies.omits: The third seed and the bootstrap confidence intervals reported in final; search scores carry more split/seed noise than the final claim.

search_proxies.name: binary_item_matrix_only
search_proxies.preserves: The binary per-item response matrices used in the final plane.
search_proxies.omits: Item text, item metadata and non-binary scores; shared models across benchmarks are not used as data, and item order and model order are shuffled by the evaluator.

search_visible: search-plane metrics.json scalars (combined_score, mae, rmse, spearman, kendall, split-level and baseline-delta metrics, control diagnostics, episode counters)
per-episode completion status and protocol-violation messages for search episodes (no target arrays, no true scores)
search benchmark opaque task_ids and the source-model matrices delivered over RPC during search episodes
search seeds and search reset sequence
final_sealed: all final-plane metrics.json values and per-episode scores
final benchmark identities, final jbl data, final seeds and seed-to-workload mapping until candidate freeze
true full scores of target models, target responses on unselected items, trusted baseline outputs and predictions on both planes' targets
final bootstrap CIs, control outcomes and claim assessment
final smoke outputs and host/evaluator resource paths

required_evidence: SHA-256 of task.md and of every staged .jbl/model-list file with the pinned upstream commit 55faff49..., verified offline; actual array shapes, per-benchmark model counts, and the check for item text/ids

split manifests (per episode: source/target model counts, strong_targets quantile rule, seeds) and the search/final disjointness report: benchmark partition, family grouping, content-hash or column-fingerprint duplicate check with its stated limitation
payload preflight of the largest request/response per plane (UTF-8 JSON bytes incl. base64, envelope, framing; all <64 MiB) and the chunk/RPC call counts versus max_candidate_rpc_calls
broker-visible reset transcript equal to the declared search/final and smoke reset sequences, one reset per episode, including controls
trusted evaluator-owned computation of every metric from held-out full-score matrices; the aggregation hierarchy and weights; retained worst-case contributions for failed/missing episodes

matched baseline results (random_mean, anchor_points_kmeans, irt_style, source_mean_constant) under identical splits, k and seeds, with record of which implementations were evaluator reimplementations versus upstream benchpred
negative-control results with non-vacuity checks (derangement verified) and expected-behaviour comparison; no causal claim if a control is vacuous or matches the real run

paired bootstrap CIs and per-benchmark/per-split breakdowns, including strong-target failure cases; claim reported as effective, ineffective, conditional or inconclusive within the k=100, CPU, binary-score bounds

enforced limits (wall clock, per-episode deadline, broker RPC cap, evaluator-enforced item budget k) explicitly distinguished from advisory candidate-internal iteration counts; smoke evidence labelled as reduced-path validation only

candidate freeze record (code digest, search ranking of the <=3 evaluations) preceding any final resource access; all numbers reproducible from submitted code with environment versions, seeds, commands and per-table/figure script mapping (paper PDF/LaTeX writing is outside this harness)
